atomicity.reason: One shall: cap the published discharge power so the current stays at 250 A while the 10 s average is at or above 250 A. The sentence on full power staying available below that average is the complement of the same condition and the closing so-clause is rationale, the same main-shall, complement, rationale shape as REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT.

comprehensibility.reason: No undefined abbreviations and the numbers are explicit, but read alone it suggests the vehicle sees 100 % power below the average. That full means the pre-limit value that is still subject to the 55-60 °C temperature derating and the 30 % actuator fallback, and that the range where drive power has to be cut back is the band of REQ_POWER_DERATING, can only be learned from sibling requirements and the architecture (minimum of three limits).
comprehensibility.suggestion: Name the sibling concepts in the text (for example the full permitted discharge power as used in REQ_POWER_DERATING) and state in one sentence that the published power is the lowest of the temperature, actuator and sustained-load limits.

feasibility.reason: A moving-average current limiter that lowers the published permitted discharge power is standard BMS practice and implementable with known technology. It contradicts neither a sibling nor REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT: the 250 A hold sits below the 350 A for 100 ms trip, and the full-power current is also below 350 A (320 A per SWREQ_SUSTAINED_LOAD_LIMIT, though this need never states it). It assumes the vehicle honours the published limit, with the 350 A trip as the hard backstop.

parent_fit.reason: US_THERMAL_MANAGEMENT says that under sustained full load (towing up a pass) the pack never draws more than its cells are rated to deliver continuously, so it does not heat into the derating range; this need holds the published power so the current stays at 250 A, the stated continuous rating, once the 10 s average shows the load is sustained. No sibling covers that clause (REQ_POWER_DERATING is temperature-driven only).

unambiguity.reason: The core rule reads one way, but four points are open: (1) engage and release share the 250 A value and, under a sustained load, the average of the capped current converges to exactly 250 A, i.e. onto the release boundary, so hold versus toggle is decided by noise or rounding; (2) it is not said how charge-direction (regen) samples enter the average, which matters on a descent after a climb; (3) the title says the BMS limits the current whereas the body limits the published power so that the current cannot exceed 250 A; (4) the sentence saying the full discharge power stays available could be misread as overriding the temperature and actuator limits.
unambiguity.suggestion: Add a release margin, as REQ_COOLING_REQUEST and REQ_HEATING_REQUEST do with their hysteresis, or state that engage and release deliberately share one threshold. Define how charge-direction samples count, align the title with the body (limit the permitted discharge power), and say the sustained-load limit is combined with the other limits by taking the minimum.

verifiability.reason: The numbers (250 A, 10 s) and the start and end conditions are explicit, but the pass criterion is on the pack current while the BMS only publishes a power, and the need gives no reference for converting one to the other (the 320 A full-power current appears only in SWREQ_SUSTAINED_LOAD_LIMIT). The phrase “from the moment” has no latency bound, the averaging method (window type, sample period, treatment of charge-direction samples) is not defined, behaviour exactly at the 250 A boundary is not defined, “short peak” is unquantified, and the clause about the pack not heating up is not testable.
verifiability.suggestion: State the oracle explicitly: published permitted discharge power at most 250 A times the present pack voltage (or give the ampere value of full power), in force within a stated maximum latency (for example one publishing cycle) of the average reaching 250 A. Define the average as the arithmetic mean of the measured pack current in the discharge direction (the quantity REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT uses) over a sliding 10 s window, and mark the clause about the pack not heating up as rationale rather than acceptance criterion.

summary: Faithful to its parent and atomic, but the need leaves the current-to-power conversion, the averaging details, the engage/release boundary and its combination with the other power limits unspecified, so it is only partly verifiable, unambiguous and self-contained.
